chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: Jo Jones's personality and other great drummers
summary: They discuss controlling Jo, whom Greene says has not changed, and compare Alvin Burroughs and Shadow Wilson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: That's right. That's right. And, then I guess Walter probably held him down as much as anyone, am I right?
Yes.

Did -- to get to Basie -- this I don't know and I'm asking you -- I mean, did Basie ever control Jo, or did he just want Jo controlled and got you guys to control him? Or did Basie, I mean, you know how Basie is. Does one ever see Basie actually give a guy an eye, or something?
No, no.
You see that, Stan? Is that right.
No -- well, you -- just the way you see Basie -- that's --
That's Basie?

That's Basie. That's the way it happens. Whatever had to be done, he had control over it at all times, more or less. As far as Jo was concerned -- we understood him -- and it wasn't a big thing as far as getting out of line, you know. Because he never got that far, because we had him covered, you know.
(laugh) His attackers.
But, I mean -- was Jo -- when you joined the band it -- was Jo much the same in terms of personality as he is today, or did he -- over the years -- become more diff--
Oh, he got worse. Didn't he Freddie?
He got worse?
He -- I don't know. I think Jo is about the same as he was back in those days.
Really, Freddie?
Well, you see, to understand him -- you have to
understand -- I understand him.
You see, alot of people don't understand Joe. But I do.
Yeah. Yeah.

You know, I understand where he's coming from. But, as far as getting out of line is concerned, I mean, like, the way he is today and yesterday -- to me, I mean -- being close to him -- I -- he's the same guy.
just --
I don't know. Well, I don't think Joe has ever really left the band.
That's where he belonged.
You see, he's never --
And, that's the trouble.
No. He's never left the band, see.
That's the trouble.
And, I realize this fact, and know why he's going through this.
Yeah. Yeah. Do you follow what Freddie's saying?
Yes, I do. And I think that -- I mean, nobody here is ever going to knock him as a drummer, but the truth is he belongs in a big band.
Definitely. (laugh)
I mean, not necessarily Basie's band, but --
No, just a big band.
-- he belongs in a big band.
Right.
Well, no other drummer, you know -- contradict me when I'm making mistakes -- but, no other drummer ever went in that band and sounded like Jo, did they?
No, no.
No one fitted or belonged in that band like him.
Well, here's the thing.
Because, now, one of the best rhythm sections was when Earl Hines had Alvin Burroughs.
Mm hmm.
That was a good rhythm section.
Mm hmm.
And George Dixon who called me in Chicago, who said that was a good rhythm section but that wasn't as good as when
Shadow did a good job over here.
Did he?
He did a terrific job over here. Yes he did.
Yeah, because his heyday was really during the war.
Oh, he was something else. He did a good job.
